requirement:
Number of hexadecimal digits in the identity hash of an anonymous selector segment.

```rust,ignore
pub const HASH_DIGITS: usize = 12;
```
rationale:
structural: The requirement prescribes a declaration: `pub const HASH_DIGITS: usize = 12;`. Its clauses are the name, the public visibility, the type `usize`, the const item form and the value 12. A `static`, a private item, a different type or a different value would break the stated declaration even if the runtime behavior looked similar. This is a structural obligation. The root `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/selector.rs#const[HASH_DIGITS]` declares exactly `pub const HASH_DIGITS: usize = 12;`. It carries the `{impl}` marker for `requirements.sdk.outlines.HASH_DIGITS`. No other roots are needed, because the declaration is the whole obligation.

behavioral: `requirements.sdk.outlines.HASH_DIGITS` states one obligation. The constant is 12, and it is the number of hexadecimal digits in the identity hash of an anonymous selector segment.

`crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement and covers both parts:
- It asserts `HASH_DIGITS == 12`, which checks the constant's value.
- It checks the anonymous `line@...` selectors on unknown-extension content. Each selector's hash part has length `HASH_DIGITS`, and every byte is an ASCII hex digit. The hash part also equals `structural_hash[..12]`, so the 12 digits are the identity hash.
- It also checks that identical lines share a selector and that different lines do not. That shows the hash identifies the segment.

The other supplied test, `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]`, only checks the public export inventory. It adds no behavioral obligation here.

No further observable obligation is left untested. Anonymous segments of other kinds would use the same single constant, so the line case is enough.
